paragraphs: Backstage smelled of dust and warm cable. Yellow Duck Sweater stood behind a velvet curtain so heavy it pressed on its head like a hand, waiting for its twenty seconds. Out front, another duck was performing the duck's own act: sit, stand, tilt, quack. Then another duck did it. Then another. The duck counted copies until the numbers went soft. In the wings a cardboard rocket sagged on its string, and the wind machine, really a small jet engine, coughed twice and gave up. Each vote landed in a jar with the click of a dropped button.

When its turn came, the stage was colder than carpet and much wider than two metres. The spotlight was the moon, round except for a thin shaving off one side, so the left edge of the stage stayed dark. The duck forgot the sit. It forgot the stand. It walked to the front, where the floor stopped at a pit, and for once the pit had something in it: a tuba and a folding chair. The duck sat on the edge and let its orange feet hang over. It sang the little song, badly, to the tuba. Somewhere in the dark, one button clicked. The moon narrowed its beam until it lit only the knitted duckling, which appeared to be taking a bow.
text:
Backstage smelled of dust and warm cable. Yellow Duck Sweater stood behind a velvet curtain so heavy it pressed on its head like a hand, waiting for its twenty seconds. Out front, another duck was performing the duck's own act: sit, stand, tilt, quack. Then another duck did it. Then another. The duck counted copies until the numbers went soft. In the wings a cardboard rocket sagged on its string, and the wind machine, really a small jet engine, coughed twice and gave up. Each vote landed in a jar with the click of a dropped button.

When its turn came, the stage was colder than carpet and much wider than two metres. The spotlight was the moon, round except for a thin shaving off one side, so the left edge of the stage stayed dark. The duck forgot the sit. It forgot the stand. It walked to the front, where the floor stopped at a pit, and for once the pit had something in it: a tuba and a folding chair. The duck sat on the edge and let its orange feet hang over. It sang the little song, badly, to the tuba. Somewhere in the dark, one button clicked. The moon narrowed its beam until it lit only the knitted duckling, which appeared to be taking a bow.
imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The duck stands backstage in the dark behind a heavy red velvet curtain that droops onto the top of its head, with coiled cables on the dusty wooden floor. Panel 2: Three ducks: the duck in the yellow sweater peeks through a gap in the red curtain at two identical robot ducks in yellow sweaters on a bright stage, one sitting and one tilting its head, while more duck-shaped shadows trail off along the back wall. Panel 3: The duck waits in the wings beside a sagging cardboard rocket hanging from a string, a small silent jet engine on a stand, and a glass jar half full of buttons. Panel 4: The duck walks out alone onto a wide, empty wooden stage lit from above by a nearly full moon hanging like a spotlight among a few thin clouds, with the left edge of the stage in shadow. Panel 5: The duck sits on the front edge of the stage with its orange feet dangling over an orchestra pit that holds one brass tuba, a music stand, and a folding chair. Panel 6: The duck sits on the edge of the stage with its head tilted back as if singing, while a narrow beam of moonlight lights only the knitted duckling on the front of its sweater and everything else is dim blue. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
